title: U.S. House · Mississippi's 4th District
area: South Mississippi, including the Gulf Coast, Hattiesburg, and the Pine Belt

context.text: Mike Ezell defeated Sawyer Walters in the March 10, 2026 Republican primary. Jeffrey Hulum III defeated Paul Blackman and D. Ryan Grover in the Democratic primary. Charles Claburn did not make the ballot for the American Independent Conservative Party.

summary.text: Mike Ezell has represented Mississippi's 4th Congressional District since 2023. He worked in law enforcement, including as sheriff of Jackson County, Mississippi, before being elected to Congress.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Southern Mississippi (1997).
Worked as a law enforcement officer.

priorities.text: His official site lists key issues including agriculture, crime and public safety, immigration and border security, jobs and the economy, national security, and veterans.

candidates.name: Jeffrey Hulum III
candidates.currentRole: Member, Mississippi House of Representatives, District 119 (since 2022)

summary.text: Jeffrey Hulum III is a current member of the Mississippi House of Representatives, representing District 119 since 2022. He served 22 years in the U.S. Army across six combat deployments, reaching the rank of sergeant major, and founded the nonprofit Extend A Hand, Help A Friend.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Army for 22 years across six combat deployments, reaching the rank of sergeant major.
Founded the nonprofit Extend A Hand, Help A Friend.
Currently serves in the Mississippi House of Representatives, District 119, since 2022.

priorities.text: "The Economy": says South Mississippi deserves an economy that works for working people, not just corporations and the wealthy.
priorities.quote: South Mississippi deserves an economy that works for working people, not just for corporations and the wealthy.

priorities.text: "Affordable Healthcare": says no family should go broke to see a doctor, citing rural hospital closures and rising costs in Mississippi.
"Quality Education": says every child deserves a quality education regardless of ZIP code.

positions.summary: Campaign website lists affordable healthcare as a priority, citing closing rural hospitals and rising costs.

summary.text: Carl Boyanton is an independent candidate for Mississippi's 4th District who previously ran for the seat in 2024, 2022, and 2020. He works in agriculture and is based on the Mississippi Gulf Coast.

background.text: Has run for Mississippi's 4th Congressional District in 2020, 2022, and 2024.

priorities.text: Says he wants to put "people over party," citing low approval ratings for both major parties.
priorities.quote: It is time to put people over party. Both parties have approval ratings under ten percent.

priorities.text: Says he will fight inflation and the cost of living by reining in federal government spending, citing the $40 trillion national debt.
Pledges to hold a town hall in every county every year if elected.

positions.summary: Survey response focuses on cutting government spending and reducing the debt rather than raising taxes.
